messages:
maria: Quick audit — AcmeCorp reports p99 TTFT spikes on a few routes. Can someone point me to the canonical panels + a couple PromQL queries I can run? Need p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec by model/route and ideally by customer slice :eyes:

raj: Start with the latency overview dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/latency/ttft-inspector — panels there are split by model, route, and customer_tag (if populated). For direct queries try these PromQL snippets:

raj: ```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_ttft_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route, customer_id))
```

raj: and tokens/sec:

raj: ```
sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (model, route, customer_id)
```

olivia: If customer_id is missing on metrics, you can still slice by injecting request attributes into logs and using the logs->metrics bridge. Quick log query (Loki):

olivia: ```
{app="runtime"} | json | customer_id="acme" | line_format "{{.route}} {{.elapsed_ms}}" | unwrap elapsed_ms
```

olivia: Also grab a trace sample in Jaeger to see cold path behavior: https://jaeger.redwood.com/search?service=runtime&minDuration=200ms&tags=route%3Dchat.generate&limit=20

sre-bot: Current alert rules: ttft_p95_alert triggers when p95(ttft) > 800ms for 5m, and ttft_p99_alert at p99 > 1500ms for 5m. :information_source:

jun: For Acme slice, add label filter to the PromQL above: replace customer_id with customer_id="acme" or use the Grafana variable. If metrics don't have labels, we should instrument route-level customer tagging in the ingress layer — filing a tiny telemetry PR helps.

jun: Quick kubectl one-liner to tail runtime logs for recent slow requests (useful if trace sampling missed it):

jun: ```
kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=runtime -c runtime --tail=200 | rg "customer_id.*acme|elapsed_ms" -n
timeout 10s
```

sam: I'll make a focused dashboard link and propose adjusted alerts. Suggestion: split alerts by customer tier — for Dedicated customers lower thresholds:

sam: - Dedicated: p95 > 600ms for 5m, p99 > 1.0s for 5m
sam: - Shared/free: p95 > 900ms for 5m, p99 > 1.5s for 5m

sam: Also add a tokens/sec saturation alert: if tokens/sec per GPU node drops below 20% of baseline for 3m, it often means throttling or queuing.

maria: Nice, can you include sample alert rule fragment for the p95 change? I'll review the PR.

sam: ```
- alert: TTFT_P95_Dedicated
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_ttft_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route, customer_tier)) > 0.6
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: critical
    tier: dedicated
  annotations:
    summary: "p95 TTFT > 600ms (dedicated)"
```

maria: Perfect. One more ask — if you can paste a grafana panel link (with variables prefilled) to the Acme slice I can forward to their SREs. :thumbsup:

raj: Pinned panel link for Acme (model=gpt-4-custom, route=chat.generate, customer_id=acme): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/latency/ttft-inspector?var-model=gpt-4-custom&var-route=chat.generate&var-customer_id=acme

olivia: I'll run a quick trace capture with 50% sample rate for that route for the next 30m and drop spans into the ticket.

maria: Awesome — thanks everyone. If we see p99 persist after these adjustments I'll open an oncall follow-up and request a capacity sweep. :rocket:
